chapter: Dew Drop and the club scene
title: George Foster's club and the first Battle of the Blues
summary: Foster's near the Dew Drop booked Roy Brown and Amos Milburn; Tex recalls Billy Wright, and the talk touches on lost records.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: What about some of the, I was talking about the ancillary clubs, and like, you know, like Foster's? How was Foster's?

George Foster was two blocks from the Doudrop, still right there on LaSalle Street. George Foster had the little downtown club, I mean the uptown club, and he wasn't the promoter that Frank Pena was. He was the guy who fell in line. But he started bringing in, like, well he had brought in Roy Brown, then he had a combination with Roy Brown, and went on the Irish with the first Battle of the Blues that I could recall in the city of New Orleans. That went on for around about maybe five hours between the two of them. And then Amos Milburn left the Dewdrop and came down to Foster's Club and Hotel, and they battled there for a while. It was a lot of fun. I'll never forget because that particular night I think Okie Doke and myself, we all went, we were just hanging out, disc jockeys hanging out together just having a good time. And I think that, let me see who else was in town at that particular time. Well, I think, well the Dewdrop had its show going with Bob Parker and Patsy Vidalia down there. And I'm trying to think of the guy from out of town who was a blues singer, and I love to listen to him. I'm trying to think of his name, it's on the tip of my tongue right now. I'm trying to think about this guy. It just doesn't come to me right now. But he was, he, tremendous blues. Billy Wright is his name. Oh, Billy Wright, from Atlanta. From Atlanta. Yeah. Blues for my baby. Right. He could let him, he could. What was his big song? Blues for my baby and You Satisfied. That was a too big, that's too big a song. Then he had.
Straight A, not straight A's. Something about Aces.
Yeah, the Aces for this. You know I'd like to get a copy of that. You know anybody who would have it?
I had a Billy Wright, I had some Billy Wright records.
I'd like to know who has it, I'd like to get a copy of that.

I don't have any Billy Wright records. I had a Billy Wright record. I have. You know my collection's in the back, and somehow, you know the years. I can understand that. Right. Something just disappears in that black hole. Right, right, right. My Billy Wright record just disappeared. Not from the archive, but before, some reason before the archive.
Well I'm glad the archives is here because we can bring them here and protect them.
Oh yeah, well that's why they're here.
I got some more stuff I gotta bring up here.
Oh, I hope so. So yeah, so Frank, so Foster's really wasn't as much competition.
